content.text:
MakerWorld is gone from the Projects & files section.

On consistency: you're right, and there's no good reason for the two to differ. I drew the Preferences Agent section without starting from the setup boards or the shipped setup code (`Setup.tsx`). Here are the actual differences:

| | Agent setup (boards and shipped code) | My Preferences boards |
|---|---|---|
| **The three ways** | "Continue with JusPrin" first, then "If you know what these are": "Use your own API key" and "Connect an AI tool you already use" | Flat lists headed "Models" and "AI tools on this computer" |
| **Choosing a provider** | Tabs: Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenRouter, one key field below | One row per provider |
| **Saved key** | "Key saved on this computer", the key's first and last characters, then Replace and Remove as links | "Key saved", the same characters, then Replace and Remove as buttons |
| **Entering a key** | Paste, Check key, "replied in 0.8 s", "Keeps sk-…a3F9" while replacing | Check key and Cancel only; no Paste, no checking or rejected states |
| **AI tools** | A list with radio buttons, "detected" or "not found", and Refresh scan | Connect and Disconnect buttons, "Found on this computer" |
| **Wording** | "Billed by your provider, not JusPrin. Stored on this machine only." | A different sentence about where keys are kept |

**What can reasonably differ** is only how much is shown at once. Setup is a guided first run inside the narrow Agent panel, so it shows one choice at a time. Preferences is where you come back to see everything you've set up. The individual pieces should be identical in both places: the three ways and their names and order, the key field and every state it can be in, the AI-tool row, and the wording.

**My recommendation:** define three shared pieces once, on the Design System page of the canvas, and use them in both places:

1. **JusPrin account:** signed out, waiting for the browser, signed in.
2. **Provider key:** no key, entering, checking, saved, replacing, rejected, and "connected but you'll need to enter it again after a restart".
3. **AI tool:** not found, detected, connected.

For keys, I'd change setup from tabs to one row per provider rather than the other way round. Tabs show one provider at a time, so you can't see which ones already have a key. That matters now that the model menu lists every provider that has one. In setup, "Use your own API key" would open the same provider rows, just narrower.

This means the change goes three ways:
- **Setup boards:** redrawn with these pieces. While doing that I'd also fix the colours typed in directly instead of taken from the design tokens, such as the green "detected" label and the green success banner.
- **Preferences:** the Agent section rebuilt with the same pieces, in setup's order and wording.
- **Code:** `Setup.tsx` changes later to match. If Preferences is built as a React page like the Agent panel, both places can use the same components, so they stay consistent in code too.

Should I go ahead with the shared pieces and redraw both setup and Preferences on the canvas? Or would you rather keep the provider tabs and have Preferences follow setup?
go ahead with provider rows and redraw both
I'll build the three shared pieces first, then redraw setup and Preferences from them. Before that, I'm reading the rest of the setup flow (the connect-a-tool steps) so the redraw covers all of it.

content.text: The setup boards are all redrawn. Next I'm converting the old "API key field" proposal board into the decided version: every key state, using the shared row, with its explanations kept.

input.content:
Your own API key · one row per provider

Decided 2026-10-21; replaces the provider tabs. Every provider has its own row, so you can see at a glance which ones have a key. Agent setup and Preferences › Agent use the same row (Design System › Agent/Provider Row). The app keeps each provider’s key on this computer and can show its start and last 4 characters; it records no dates, so none are shown. Key characters are examples.
1. No key
Only Add key. Nothing looks filled in.
2. Entering a key
Placeholder text only, no bullets: an empty field never looks filled in. Paste sits in the field; Check key waits for a key.
3. Checking
The key being checked stays visible and locked, so it is clear which one is in question. Cancel stops the check.
4. Couldn’t check
The provider couldn’t be reached. Nothing was saved, so this isn’t a rejection.
5. Key saved
A saved key is read-only: its start and last 4 characters at full contrast. It never shows as bullets.
6. Replacing
Replace opens an empty field for the new key. The saved key stays until the new one passes its check; Cancel keeps it.
7. Rejected
The provider refused the saved key. Its last 4 characters stay visible so the person knows which key failed.
8. Working until restart
The key passed but couldn’t be stored on this computer. It works now and will be asked for again after a restart.

input.title: Match Agent setup code to the provider-row design
input.prompt:
Update the shipped Agent setup UI in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Setup.tsx` (and its CSS and tests) to match the redesigned boards on the "JusPrin v2" canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), decided 2026-10-21.

What changed in the design:
- "Your own API key" no longer uses provider tabs (`setup-tabs`, role=tablist). It shows one row per provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter). Each row has a name, a status line and actions. States: no key (Add key); entering (field with Paste inside, Check key, Cancel); checking (key locked, "Checking with <provider>…", Cancel); couldn't check (danger text, nothing saved); saved ("Key saved on this computer" plus the start…last-4 hint, Replace and Remove buttons); replacing ("Keeps <hint> until the new key passes"); rejected; working until restart (the current "partial" warning). The design source is the canvas files `project/agent-row-provider.dc.html` and `project/agent-group-keys.dc.html`, plus the states board `project/agent-setup-api-key-saved-vs-empty-proposal.dc.html`.
- The chooser shows the JusPrin account as a block ("JusPrin account", "Free · sign in with your browser · nothing to install", primary button "Continue with JusPrin"). See `project/agent-row-account.dc.html` and `project/agent-setup-setup-agent-main.dc.html`.
- The AI tool list uses rows with a "Connect…" button per tool instead of radio buttons, and "Look again" instead of "Refresh scan". See `project/agent-row-tool.dc.html` and `project/agent-group-tools.dc.html`.
- The success banner uses tokens, not hard-coded greens.

Read the canvas files with the Artifact tool (read action with `path`). Follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` "Writing UI code": colours, radii and fonts come from tokens, and a value with no token gets a token first. Build the rows as reusable React components so a later Preferences page can use the same ones. Done means: the setup screens match the boards, `npm test` passes in AgentUI, and you have checked it in the running app. Don't commit unless asked.
input.background: JusPrin is an AI-piloted fork of OrcaSlicer. On 2026-10-21 Kenneth decided that the Agent's connection UI must look and behave the same in Agent setup (the docked Agent panel, React in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`) and in a new JusPrin Preferences window (designed on the canvas, not built yet). Three shared pieces were designed: the JusPrin account block, a provider key row (one row per provider, replacing tabs), and an AI tool row, plus shared tool-connection steps. Setup shows one way at a time; Preferences › Agent shows all three. The canvas is the design source of truth (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, rule 5). JusPrin account sign-in isn't implemented in code yet; keep its button disabled as today unless that code exists.

content.text:
I've redrawn Agent setup and Preferences on the [JusPrin v2 canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v) so both use the same parts. I haven't opened the canvas to look at the result, because the canvas's rules say not to unless you ask. Tell me if you want me to go through it.

**Shared parts.** These are on the Design System page under "Agent connection". Setup and Preferences both use these files directly, so a change to one shows up in both places.
- **JusPrin account:** signed out ("Continue with JusPrin"), waiting for the browser, signed in, and signed in with the Agent unavailable.
- **Provider key row:** one row per provider, with no tabs. It covers no key, entering, checking, couldn't check, saved, replacing (the old key is kept until the new one passes), rejected, and working until restart.
- **AI tool row:** not found, found, connected. The group around the rows ends with a "Look again" button.
- **Tool connection steps:** the Claude Code command, the Cursor review, saving, done, and the error states. Preferences uses the same steps as setup.
- **A board showing every state** of all of these, in light and dark.

**Agent setup.** All 14 boards keep their place and file names but are now built from the shared parts. The old "API key field" proposal board is now the decided version: all eight key states, each with its explanation. I also replaced the colours that were typed in directly instead of taken from the tokens (the green "detected" label, the green banner and the grey composer border).

**Preferences.**
- **Agent section:** follows setup's order and wording. That is JusPrin account, then "Your own API key", then "Connect an AI tool you already use", then the default model for new chats.
- **Account section:** uses the same account block.
- **New board:** "Agent › connecting Cursor" shows the same connection steps opening inside the Preferences window.
- **Headings:** group headings in every section now use the same sentence-case style, replacing the uppercase labels.

**Small wording changes from the old setup boards:**
- "Refresh scan" is now "Look again".
- Tool rows have a "Connect…" button instead of radio buttons.
- The old "replied in 0.8 s" message is gone. A key that passes simply shows as saved.

The shipped setup code still uses provider tabs. I've left a card for a session that brings `Setup.tsx` in line with these boards and builds the rows as reusable components, so a Preferences page in code can use them too. Nothing runs until you start it.
check the auto-slice task chip for the decision.

The auto-slice session's decision: **JusPrin slices the active plate on its own, about 2 seconds after the last change. You don't press Slice, and there's no setting for it.** The session has already started building this (it's going further than the decision), but nothing is compiled, tested or committed yet. All the changes are in JusPrin's own files, with no OrcaSlicer file touched.

How the drafted version behaves:
- **When it waits:** while you're dragging, while a tool other than Move, Rotate or Scale is open, while another slice or an arrange job is running, while you're not looking at Prepare, and while the Agent is mid-turn. A run of Agent edits therefore produces a single slice at the end.
- **After a cancel or failure:** it doesn't try again until something changes.
- **Quiet in the chat:** an automatic slice doesn't post a "Slicing…" card or open the chat panel.
- **Taking over:** if you press Slice, or the Agent asks to slice, while an automatic slice is running, that request takes over the running slice instead of being refused.

What's still open:
- **Not built or run yet:** the build was still in progress, and the new tests (a unit test and a full-app scenario) haven't run.
- **Failures it found:** the app's main automated test scenario already fails 7 checks before this change, on window resizing and autosave, so those failures aren't from this work.
- **Error pop-up:** a badly failing automatic slice still shows OrcaSlicer's error dialog. The session suggests stopping that as a separate piece of work.

This fits the Preferences design, which has no auto-slice setting. Details are in [Decide how JusPrin handles auto-slice](#local_ac606645-e5c4-4125-a689-7896a5b8072a).

The auto-slice session ([Decide how JusPrin handles auto-slice](#local_ac606645-e5c4-4125-a689-7896a5b8072a)) found why the automatic slice sometimes never started and has fixed it. A full test run of the fix is going now and hasn't reported a result.

The cause was a timing gap, not something restarting the 2-second wait. JusPrin checks the plate about every 33 ms. In one failing run, the test scaled the cube within a single one of those checks after the previous slice finished. The automatic-slice code never noticed the plate had been sliced, so it didn't see that the scale made that slice out of date. It treated the plate as already tried and stopped.

The fix, in `AutoSlice.cpp`, records the plate as sliced the moment a slice finishes, instead of waiting for the next check. Everything is still uncommitted.

22	- The permission guard refuses `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` (it reports it as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. Hand build-tree deletion to the user; build trees there contain `resources` symlinks into live worktrees, so unlink those before any recursive delete.
23	- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
24	- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
25	- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
26	- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].
27	
28	Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
29	`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
30	PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
31	session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.
32	
33	npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
34	TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
35	Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
36	`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
37	bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
38	FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
39	`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.
40	
41	The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
42	a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.
43	
44	To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
45	can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
46	(skips the npm requirement above) plus
47	`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
48	`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
49	bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
50	`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
51	and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
52	`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.
53	
54	An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
55	in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
56	configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
57	`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
58	is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
59	PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.
60	
61	**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
62	`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;
63	a link there holds `.lib` files and breaks their build (LNK1104). Use a separate tree instead: configure
64	with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`
65	at a short path such as `C:\b\wsh`, which is a full `libslic3r_gui` build of about 40 minutes. To symbolize a crash
66	without a debugger, relink with a `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` props file (Link `GenerateDebugInformation`/`GenerateMapFile`),
67	read the fault offset from the event log (Application, event 1000), and run
68	`llvm-symbolizer --obj=<exe> --relative-address <offset>` (the symbolizer ships in the MSVC bin dir).
69	
70	- The in-app browser pane renders a `file://` page as a static snapshot and refuses `screenshot`.
71	  To look at a rendered page (e.g. a vitest `PREVIEW_OUT` page), serve the directory over a
72	  throwaway node http server on 127.0.0.1 and navigate to that instead.
73	
74	**Commits can hang in the `entire` hook (2026-09-25):** `git commit` from an agent session in a worktree
75	never returned; `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` alone hangs too (60 s, no output,
76	stdin closed). `--no-verify` does not skip prepare-commit-msg, and hooks must not be bypassed anyway, so
77	stop after one timed attempt (`timeout 90 git commit ... < /dev/null`), kill the orphaned `entire`
78	process it leaves behind (`ps -W | grep entire`), and ask Kenneth. Other sessions' commits carry an
79	`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, so the hook works somewhere; the cause was not found.
80	
81	**Concurrent harness runs collide on WebView2 (2026-09-25):** every harness exe uses the same WebView2
82	profile, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JusPrin2\EBWebView`. While another session's harness is running (e.g. a
83	long `--home-printers-live` fixture run), a second harness fails at once with
84	`shell_agent_page_handshake_complete FAIL`, and its app log shows `JusPrin agent page failed to load:
85	The group or resource is not in the correct state`. That is not a page or bundle problem. Check for
86	`shell_integration_harness.exe` in `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, don't kill another session's
87	process, and set `$env:WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER='C:\b\<tree>-webview'` for your own runs.
88	
89	**Scripting on this box (2026-10-06; Python corrected 2026-10-21):** no `python`/`py` on PATH, but Python 3.13 is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\python-3.13.9\python.exe` and runs the prompt suites (`tests/project_prompt`, set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` and `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`). Otherwise use node (`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). Bash heredocs and `node -e "..."` that contain backticks, `${...}` or backslashes get mangled by the shell; write the script to a file with the Write tool and run `node <file>`. The main checkout's build tree `C:\src\JusPrin\build` (VS generator, Release) is fine to build from a session that is working in the main checkout: `cmake --build C:\src\JusPrin\build --config Release --target <targets> -- -m` after `vcvars64.bat`; harness exes there read `resources\` from the source tree, so `npm run build` in `AgentUI` is enough to refresh the Agent page. A touched `Workspace.hpp` rebuild of `libslic3r_gui` + `shell_integration_harness` takes roughly 10 minutes.

Some of what I told you earlier was wrong or incomplete:

- **I called the Preferences window "finished".** It wasn't. Its language fix changed OrcaSlicer's own web-page code, which the fork-stewardship rules discourage, and a real restart avoids that. I passed its report on without checking.
- **I made the update window that pops up at startup your problem.** I said "if you see it, that's a known problem". It's a bug we should fix, not one for you to work around.
- **The test build I launched blocked the Preferences session.** It ran from that session's own build tree, which stopped it rebuilding, and you were asked to close it. I should have run it from a separate copy.

Where things stand now:

**Preferences window** ([Build the JusPrin Preferences window](#local_03e4175d-0a29-4d34-b76e-359fa9635186)): it now uses the restart approach, committed as `377e1f58e1` on `claude/musing-wing-e808a9`.
- **OrcaSlicer's files:** only a 6-line hook in `GUI_App` is left. The `WebView` and wipe-tower changes are reverted.
- **Picking a language:** it shows "JusPrin will use Deutsch after it restarts", with **Restart now** and **Later**. Restart now starts a fresh JusPrin with the same data folder.
- **Tested:** three language switches, plus one from Prepare.

It left two paths untested, and I've told it to test them now rather than leave them to you:
- restarting while a project with a real model and unsaved edits is open;
- cancelling at the unsaved-changes question.

It will fix anything that fails and leave the build ready. Then I'll launch it for you from a separate copy, so nothing gets locked again. macOS and Linux can't be checked on this machine. That's a limit of this machine, not something for you to check.

**Update check** ([Design JusPrin's own update check](#local_6d12e3c2-d1ec-4939-9214-7be5e8398a61)): the Updates design is on the canvas.
- **The startup pop-up:** I've told it to fix the OrcaSlicer update window that opens at startup on its own branch. It should use JusPrin's own files where possible, and confirm in the running app that the window is gone.

Two decisions are genuinely yours:

1. **How "new version" works at first.**
   - My recommendation: **Download** simply opens the GitHub release page, and installing inside the app comes later.
   - Why: installing inside the app is a lot of new work for each platform (Windows installer, macOS disk image, portable copies).
2. **JusPrin's first v2 version number.** It has to be above v1's 1.4.0. My recommendation is **2.0.0**. Today the app reports OrcaSlicer's 2.4.2, so the update check can't compare versions properly until this is set.

I'll report back when both sessions finish, then launch the Preferences build for you to test.
was the page built with webview, or?

Yes. The Preferences window is a native window with a web view inside it, the same setup as the Agent panel.

- **The page:** it's React, built as part of the Agent page bundle (`AgentUI`, output to `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`). The Preferences session's test scripts click page elements like `.prefs-nav-item` through the web view's DevTools.
- **The window:** `Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp` is native C++. It hosts the web view, sends the page the current settings, and handles what the page sends back, like saving a setting or closing.
- **Settings:** the C++ side owns them. It reads and writes the app's config, so classic view and JusPrin always agree. The page only draws what C++ tells it and sends requests.

This web view is also why language switching broke at first. All the app's web pages share one Edge browser process, and Edge won't start a page in a new language while that process is still running with the old one. Restarting the app avoids that, which is why the Preferences session switched to restarting on a language change.

content.text:
Yes. Preferences and Agent setup use the same components from one file, [AgentConnection.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx), on the Preferences branch:

- **Preferences** (`Preferences.tsx`) imports `AccountRow`, `ProviderKeys` and `ToolGroup`.
- **Agent setup** (`Setup.tsx`) imports `AccountRow` and `ProviderKeys`.
- **The tool list in setup** (`SetupLocalTool.tsx`) imports `ToolGroup`.

So the account block, the provider key rows and the AI tool list are one implementation each. A change to a row shows up in both places, matching how the shared pieces are set up on the canvas.
